stage_b_review_note: Pinned dpa.tex 150–161 and proof-safe Definition at 35–47 give five divided-power axioms. If maps γ_n on I satisfy identity, scalar homogeneity and addition universally, and multiplicative-binomial law plus iterated divided-power law merely on ideal generators, then they form DP structure. Stage A's explicit five formulas match the safe definition and retain the different universal/generator scopes.
statement:
The five divided power axioms on an ideal $I$ of a commutative ring $A$, for all $x,y\in I$, $a\in A$, $m,n>0$, are (1) $\gamma_1(x)=x$, $\gamma_0(x)=1$; (2) $\gamma_n(x)\gamma_m(x)=\binom{n+m}{n}\gamma_{n+m}(x)$; (3) $\gamma_n(ax)=a^n\gamma_n(x)$; (4) $\gamma_n(x+y)=\sum_{i=0}^n\gamma_i(x)\gamma_{n-i}(y)$; (5) $\gamma_n(\gamma_m(x))=\frac{(nm)!}{n!(m!)^n}\gamma_{nm}(x)$ (dpa.tex L37–46).
Let $A$ be a ring. Let $I$ be an ideal of $A$. Let $\gamma_n : I \to I$,
$n \geq 1$ be a sequence of maps. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] (1), (3), and (4) of the five divided-power axioms listed in the context note
hold for all $x, y \in I$, and
\item[(b)] properties (2) and (5) hold for $x$ in
some set of generators of $I$ as an ideal.
\end{enumerate}
Then $\gamma$ is a divided power structure on $I$.
Here properties (1), (3), (4) in the referenced definition are the identity, scalar-power, and addition laws; properties (2), (5) are the multiplication and iteration laws of divided powers (dpa.tex L38–55).

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-two-ideals}
Let $A$ be a ring with two ideals $I, J \subset A$.
Let $\gamma$ be a divided power structure on $I$ and let
$\delta$ be a divided power structure on $J$.
Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\gamma$ and $\delta$ agree on $IJ$,
\item if $\gamma$ and $\delta$ agree on $I \cap J$ then they are
the restriction of a unique divided power structure $\epsilon$
on $I + J$.
\end{enumerate}
stage_b_review_note: Original 232–244: DP structures γ on I and δ on J always agree on IJ. If they also agree on I∩J, a UNIQUE DP structure ε on I+J restricts to each. The draft preserves unconditional first clause and conditional second clause without asserting every pair glues.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-nil}
Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $A$ be a ring, let $I \subset A$ be an ideal,
and let $\gamma$ be a divided power structure on $I$. Assume $p$ is nilpotent
in $A/I$. Then $I$ is locally nilpotent if and only if $p$ is nilpotent in $A$.
stage_b_review_note: Pinned 314–319: p prime, I DP ideal in commutative A, p nilpotent mod I, then I locally nilpotent IFF p nilpotent in A. The preparation preserves both directions and does not mistake local nilpotence for uniform nilpotence.
